newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian cabinet rejects Vakaru Bank rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian cabinet rejects Vakaru Bank rescue plan.

text.p: The Lithuanian cabinet on Friday rejected a plan proposed by the transportation ministry to rescue the troubled Vakaru (West) Bank, a government spokesman told Reuters.

The bank, the eighth largest in the Baltic state with assets worth over 200 million litas, was brought down by a crippling bad loan portfolio. Most of its operations were suspended at the start of this year.
The bank had put forward a plan for recapitalisation which included a government guarantee for a $70 million loan.
It had also requested that one of its clients, the state-run Klaipeda State Seaport Authority, transform a frozen 20 million litas deposit into share capital.
Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius had said earlier this month that it would be far less costly to let the bank go bankrupt than pay for its recovery.

The bank's assets as of July 1 were worth 211.7 million litas, while its capital adequacy requirement was negative at minus 6.77 percent and its liquidity rato was 15.18 percent, far below the Bank of Lithuania's minimum requirement of 30 percent.
"The Bank of Lithuania should shortly revoke the bank's license and initiate bankruptcy proceedings," Finance Minister Algimantas Krizinauskas was quoted as saying by the local Baltic News Service.
Lithuania is still recovering from the effects of a banking crisis last year with the surprise closure of two of its top banks, Litimpeks and Innovation.
Litimpeks has since been reopened but Innovation is being nationalised as part of a costly government rescue plan.
A fresh crisis in the sector was recently averted when the government decided to bail out the troubled state-run State Commercial Bank with a special 90 million litas bond.
Lithuanians remain deeply suspicious of their infant banking system. Only three percent of the those questioned in a recent poll expressed trust in the country's commercial banks.
